Evidence / CLM-039
Evidence record
When was it measured or observed?World Bank public data interfaces as reviewed on 10 September 2026, and earlier documented access
Who or what does it apply to?Specific to each source or display interface

A public interface is not the same thing as the underlying dataset

01What does this evidence establish?

World Bank public remittance interfaces do not expose Yemen history uniformly. One interface, reviewed on 10 September 2026, showed an older span of years, while other World Bank interfaces and earlier documented retrievals contained later observations. The difference reflects what each interface displays and how its data can be traced; it is not evidence that later underlying data are absent.

01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

The difference, as reviewed on 10 September 2026, between the span of Yemen remittance observations shown on one World Bank public data interface and the later observations on other World Bank interfaces and in earlier documented access.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Specific to each source or display interface

04How current is it?

The interfaces were reviewed on 10 September 2026, and what each shows may have changed since. The record should not be read as describing a later state of the interfaces unless they are reviewed again.

05What this evidence does not establish

The difference does not show that data were deleted or withdrawn, or why any correction was made, and one public interface's observations are not a substitute for another's.

Limits of the measure

What one interface shows does not establish that the underlying data are absent or deleted, or why they were revised.
